upgrades.notes:
Bring this site onto the current Landlight template **without changing how it looks or what it says**. Work in a copy, never in production.

0. A copy reopens from its branch and builds it first, and the copy's tools only start once that build passes. Until `npm run build` succeeds, commit on a branch named `$RQEIM_WORK_BRANCH-upgrade` and push there; push the work branch only when the build passes.
1. Fetch the template: `git remote add template https://github.com/RqeimCloud/landlight.js.git && git fetch template main`.
2. Take these from `template/main` as they are: `scripts/`, `vite.config.js`, `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`, `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore`, `src/app.js`, `src/alpine.js`, `src/webmcp.js`, `prompts/`, `.agent/`, `AGENTS.md`. Then merge `package.json`: keep the site's own extra dependencies, take the template's scripts and dependencies, and run `npm install` to rewrite `package-lock.json`. The lock must not contain `git+ssh`.
3. Move every page to `src/views/<path>.html`. `src/pages/` is now generated and git-ignored: delete the old copy from git. A site in one language may keep its text in the views. A site in two or more languages has one view per page, its words in `src/locales/<locale>.json` with `{{t:key}}`, and one copy of each component using the same tokens. Read `.agent/PAGES.md` first. Text that JavaScript writes (`data-i18n`, `x-text` from a store, a list built by `x-for`) becomes static HTML with tokens; a language button becomes a link to `{{locale:<code>}}`; every page needs `<main id="main">`, a skip link to `#main`, and a `404` view. Remove scripts that read or store the language.
4. Merge `site.config.json` with the template's: keep every value of this site, add the new fields (`locales` with each language's `og`, name and description, and `exceptions: {}`). Its `url`, `email`, names and colours are this site's, never the template's.
5. Images and fonts: put the originals and the logo (`media/logo.svg`) in `media/`, run `npm run assets`, and use the WebP files it writes; without a logo the icons stay Landlight's. Fonts from Google move to `src/public/fonts/` (see `prompts/02-design.md`). Keep the same pictures and faces.
6. Run `npm run verify` until it ends in `VERIFY PASSED`. Lighthouse 90 in every category is the aim, not a gate: fix what it lists with `prompts/04-verify.md`, and name any score still under 90 in your report. The gate does need what only the owner knows: privacy and terms pages linked from the footer, and a real address for every `href="#"`. Ask for each one that is missing, and for a real email and phone if `site.config.json` has none. A meta description under 120 characters may be lengthened without changing its meaning.
7. Compare the copy's preview with production at 375px and 1440px, page by page and language by language: same layout, same text, same links. Only then, with the owner's permission, publish it and record version 1.

Zero-downtime deploys need a health check. In `Dockerfile`, right after `EXPOSE 80`, add the template's two lines:

```
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD wget -q -O /dev/null http://127.0.0.1/ || exit 1
```

If this site changed its nginx `listen` port, use that port. Check the copy builds and its preview answers, then publish with the owner's permission and record version 2.

The template now builds, runs its dev server and its scripts with Bun instead of Node and npm: faster and lighter inside a small development copy. nginx still serves production and the image does not grow. Work in a copy, never in production.

1. Install the tools in the copy first (it runs the production image: nginx on Alpine, no Node, no Bun): take `scripts/setup-copy.sh` from the template (step 2 fetches it: `git checkout template/main -- scripts/setup-copy.sh`) and run `sh scripts/setup-copy.sh`; run it again whenever the copy restarts. Lighthouse needs memory: ask the user for size m or larger for the copy before `bun run verify`.
2. Fetch the template: `git remote add template https://github.com/RqeimCloud/landlight.js.git && git fetch template main`. Take `Dockerfile` (its build stage is `FROM oven/bun:<pinned>-alpine`, which already has Bun: never install Bun in a Dockerfile with the install script, since that image path lacks bash and unzip and the build fails with `bash: not found`; if this site's Dockerfile runs extra checks in its build, such as Lighthouse, keep them but start that stage from the template's `oven/bun` line and add `apk add --no-cache nodejs chromium` there), `scripts/verify.mjs`, `.gitignore` and the docs (`AGENTS.md`, `prompts/`, `.agent/`) from `template/main` as they are. If the site changed its nginx `listen` port, keep the port in the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK.
3. In `package.json` switch the scripts: `verify` → `bun scripts/verify.mjs`, `indexnow` → `bun scripts/indexnow.mjs`, `assets` → `bun add --no-save sharp@0.35.5 svgo@4.1.0 && bun scripts/assets.mjs`. Keep the site's own dependencies.
4. Replace `package-lock.json` with `bun.lock`: delete `package-lock.json` (`git rm`), run `bun install`, and commit `bun.lock`. The lock must not contain `git+ssh`.
5. Build with `bun run build`, then run `bun run verify` until it ends in `VERIFY PASSED`, and check the copy's preview. Then, with the owner's permission, publish it and record version 3.

The template's own design changed: deep night and champagne gold, with a light and a dark theme, a three-part footer and a theme switch in the header. **Nothing here is forced on a site that already has its own look:** an existing site keeps its fonts, colours and pages, and this update is only taken when the owner asks for it. New sites start from it, so this is what `list_templates` shows.

If the owner does want it, work in a copy, never in production, and keep every word of the site:

1. `sh scripts/setup-copy.sh` (Bun, Node, Chromium) and run it again after the copy restarts.
2. Fetch the template: `git remote add template https://github.com/RqeimCloud/landlight.js.git && git fetch template main`.
3. Take as they are: `src/app.css`, `src/components/{header,footer,theme}.html`, `src/public/fonts/`, `src/app.js`, `nginx.conf`, `scripts/`, `.agent/`, `prompts/`. Merge `package.json` (the template's scripts and dependencies, plus the site's own) and run `bun install`.
4. Every page gets `<include src="src/components/theme.html"></include>` as the first thing in `<head>`, and its `<main>` must be `<main id="main">`; the skip link lives in the header partial.
5. The design's words are new keys: `brand.*`, `nav.*`, `hero.*`, `features.*`, `how.*`, `cta.*`, `footer.*`, `ui.*`. Write them in the site's own voice in `src/locales/<locale>.json`; the copy fails the build while a key is missing, and that is the list to work through page by page.
6. Colours: keep the site's brand in `--gold` and `--gold-ink` (both must be readable: `--gold-ink` is the one used for text), and set `brand.theme` / `brand.themeLight` in `site.config.json` to match.
7. `bun run verify` until `VERIFY PASSED`, then compare the preview with production at 375px and 1440px, in both themes, and publish only with the owner's permission.

A site that stays on its own design can still take the cheap wins alone: the skip link, the two `theme-color` meta tags, the `/fonts/` cache rule in `nginx.conf`, and `font-display: optional` on its largest headline.

description.ar: موقع سريع بأفضل الممارسات: وصولية عالية، وتحسين لمحركات البحث، وصفحات يفهمها وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي، بلغة واحدة أو أكثر، بوضعين فاتح وداكن. للمواقع التعريفية وصفحات الهبوط والمحتوى، بلا قاعدة بيانات.
description.en: A fast website built on best practice: high accessibility, search engine optimisation and pages AI agents can read, in one language or more, in a light and a dark theme. For company sites, landing pages and content, with no database.
